title: Specificity Index Statistic
text: pSI calculates Specificity Index (pSI) statistic, identifies genes enriched specific cell types tissues matrix expression profiles, performs Cell type-Specific Expression Analysis (CSEA): testing whether candidate gene list, example genes associated disorder, -represented among genes specific cell type. method comes Dougherty lab Washington University St. Louis.

title: Specificity Index Statistic
text: CRAN (version 1.2.0 accepted): development version, GitHub:
code: install.packages("pSI") # install.packages("pak") pak::pak("DunderChief/pSI")

title: Specificity Index Statistic
text: See ?specificity.index statistic parameters, package website full reference.
code: library(pSI)  # 1. Compute pSI values from an expression matrix: genes in rows, cell types #    (or tissues, or brain regions) in columns. The bundled sample.data$pSI.input #    is BrainSpan RNA-seq data for six adult brain regions. set.seed(1) psi <- specificity.index(pSI.in = sample.data$pSI.input, e_min = 20)  # 2. Which genes are specific to each region, and how many, at the four #    standard pSI thresholds (0.05, 0.01, 0.001, 0.0001)? specific_genes <- pSI.list(sample.data$pSI.output) pSI.count(sample.data$pSI.output)  # 3. CSEA: is a candidate gene list enriched among the genes specific to any #    region? Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-values from Fisher's exact test ... fisher.iteration(sample.data$pSI.output, candidate.genes$AutDB) # ... and the overlapping genes themselves candidate.overlap(sample.data$pSI.output, candidate.genes$AutDB)

title: Specificity Index Statistic
text: Precomputed pSI tables 35 mouse cell types (bacTRAP, October 2013) human brain regions across development (BrainSpan), used CSEA paper, distributed companion package pSI.data. 10 MB never CRAN. now live GitHub release repository, unchanged 2014 originals, package fetches demand: psi_data() verifies download checksum returns NULL message, rather error, files fetched. See ?psi_data two lists contain caching works.
code: mouse <- psi_data("mouse")   # asks once whether to keep a local copy human <- psi_data("human")  # CSEA of a candidate list against the 35 mouse cell types fisher.iteration(mouse$psi.out, candidate.genes$AutDB)

text: pSIs data frame output specificity.index, one column per cell type/sample genes rows. candidate.genes character vector official gene symbols test -representation. background character string naming background gene list test. default "data.set" uses genes pSIs; use candidate genes pSI data set come species. "human.mouse" restricts background genes pSIs (human) clear mouse homolog, testing mouse candidate list human pSI data set; "mouse.human" converse. two options download UCSC kgXref table mm10 hg19 (file several megabytes) https://hgdownload.soe.ucsc.edu/ stop informative error download fails. p.adjust logical. title: pSI: Specificity Index Statistic — pSI-package
text: Tools Specificity Index (pSI) statistic, identifies genes enriched specific cell types tissues matrix expression profiles, Cell type-Specific Expression Analysis (CSEA) candidate gene lists. typical workflow : specificity.index computes pSI values expression     matrix genes rows cell types/samples columns. pSI.list pSI.count list count     genes specific cell type four pSI thresholds     (0.05, 0.01, 0.001, 0.0001). candidate.overlap fisher.iteration     intersect candidate gene list specific genes test     overlap significance Fisher's exact test. title: Specificity Index Statistic — specificity.index
text: specificity.index calculates specificity index statistic (pSI) every gene every cell type/sample expression matrix. pSI identifies genes enriched specific cell populations across large number profiles, correctly predicts situ hybridization patterns many cell types (Dougherty et al. 2010).

title: Specificity Index Statistic — specificity.index
text: cell type 1 gene \(n\), specificity index mean, \(m-1\) cell types \(k\), rank (among genes) expression ratio gene cell type 1 cell type \(k\): $$SI_{n,1}=  \frac{ \sum_{k=2}^m rank( \frac{ IP_{1,n} }{ IP_{k,n} })  }{m-1}$$ low SI means gene highly enriched cell type 1 relative others. pSI p-value observed SI, obtained comparing null distribution SI values computed bts expression matrices resampled replacement. save time calculated genes whose p-value p_max; genes, genes expression e_min set NA pSI..filter, returned NA. null distribution resampled, results vary slightly run run; call set.seed first reproducible result.
